page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 compute instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance provides 16 physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. Cores are dedicated rather than shared, utilizing two threads per physical core to ensure predictable compute performance across concurrent execution pipelines.

The server is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. There is no local storage included with this instance profile, requiring persistent storage workloads to rely on remote block volume storage configurations. Additionally, the instance does not feature dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs, focusing its physical resource allocation exclusively on system memory and multi-threaded CPU throughput. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the virtual machine.

From an efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU allocation reduces resource waste in memory-bound architectures where processing demands are steady rather than overwhelmingly compute-heavy. Operating without bundled local drives allows provisioning flexibility, avoiding the cost overhead of unneeded local NVMe storage if external volumes suffice. This configuration is suitable for medium-to-large in-memory caching solutions, enterprise database management systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise application serving.
